findingDetails.title: process_start is mapped onto the shell shape without a recorded tool_input key, so every shell guard fails open on a background command
findingDetails.scopeProof: the mapping is the single seam every shell-shaped guard reads; six call sites consume call.input.command
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: a captured process_start payload whose tool_input carries command

findingDetails.title: The spec gate's advisory reply uses a field the reference documents only for session_start, on a hook declared strict
findingDetails.scopeProof: spec-gate.mjs:72-78 is the only advise branch in the bundle

findingDetails.title: The compaction post-tool binding injects the operator's goal slice into subagent sessions, while the hand-over part in the same hook excludes them
findingDetails.scopeProof: compaction-post-tool.mjs is the only binding with no match that composes a context part

findingDetails.title: Two cwd conventions split the adapters, so a relative payload cwd resolves differently depending on which hook reads it
findingDetails.scopeProof: the two groups are exhaustive over the 27 reviewed files

findingDetails.title: The Vibe session-cleanup hook imports the OpenCode plugin module directly, contradicting the documented re-expression and coupling a Vibe binding to a mirror surface
findingDetails.scopeProof: session-cleanup.mjs:16 is the only import of a .opencode/ module in the 27 reviewed files

findingDetails.title: overlay-guard is registered for bash and process_start but its own tool filter allows both, so the binding costs a process spawn per shell call and guards nothing
findingDetails.scopeProof: overlay-guard.mjs is the only strict pre_tool guard whose match names a tool its own filter rejects

results.summary: The documented binding census and strict set match the file exactly: 18 bindings, 2 pre_agent, 7 strict pre_tool, 6 post_tool, 1 post_agent, 1 session_start, 1 session_end.
The declared target is a file set, not a spec folder with a checklist; the disposition table is an exclusion list, not a checklist to verify.

noveltyJustification: First iteration of the lineage, so every finding is new: weightedNew = 5 (P1) + 5x1 (P2) = 10 against weightedTotal 10. No prior finding was refined or repeated.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: 27 hook and plugin files across two runtimes, with a security-relevant fail-open seam and a documented wire format to check against

targetSelection.selectionReason: the shared payload seam plus the bindings whose payload field or reply channel is unverified

searchLedger.hypothesis: process_start carries a tool_input key other than command, so the shell guards see an empty command

searchActions.result: only the match selector and the CORE_TOOL_NAMES entry name it; no captured payload and no documented key

searchLedger.rationale: the assumption is unverified and the failure direction is allow

searchLedger.hypothesis: the advise reply is a schema mismatch on a strict hook and becomes a deny

searchActions.result: advise is reachable for bash when the gate is open and the notice is undelivered

searchLedger.rationale: reachable, but the reply shape's acceptance is unverified and live evidence shows a strict hook tolerating a non-deny object

searchLedger.hypothesis: tool_status is absent from the post_tool payload, so the failed-tool guard never fires

searchActions.result: tool_status is a documented post_tool field

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: the field is documented for post_tool

searchLedger.hypothesis: the partial context passed to the OpenCode plugin breaks the startup guards

searchActions.result: the inner server reads input.worktree || input.directory || REPO_ROOT, so { worktree } is sufficient today

searchLedger.rationale: the runtime break is ruled out but the coupling to a mirror surface and to two undocumented internals remains

searchLedger.hypothesis: the bash registration is dead because the hook's own filter rejects bash

searchActions.result: WRITE_TOOLS is write and edit only, and line 42 returns allow for anything else

searchLedger.rationale: confirmed by direct read; the OpenCode plugin has the same filter, so only the match is wrong
